summary: Request access for Support/CS to overload protection dashboards + circuit breaker runbooks
description:
Request type: Access / RBAC

Requestor: Support/CS (Support Readiness)
Requested by: Dev Patel

Background
We are in canary rollout of Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding). Support is seeing new customer-visible overload errors (429/503 + overload codes) and needs direct visibility into the new dashboards + runbooks to:
- answer customer questions quickly (what happened, whether Retry-After was sent, whether a region/model was saturated)
- determine whether to escalate to SRE vs Routing vs Runtime
- avoid asking Eng for screenshots during peak incidents

Access requested
1) Dashboards (Grafana / Observability Pack)
- "Hosted Overload Protection – Overview" (shed rate, breaker-open rate, retry-after coverage)
- "Runtime Saturation – Queue Depth & Tokens/sec" (aggregated)
- "Gateway Admission – Rejects/429s" (by region, tier)

2) Runbooks (Confluence)
- Hosted overload circuit breaker runbook
- Runtime overload mitigation runbook (read-only)

Users / groups
Primary: Support + CS escalation oncall rotation
Proposed RBAC groups:
- okta-group: support-cs
- grafana-role: rbac-observability-overload-viewer (new)
- confluence-space permission: SUPPORT (read-only) for the runbook pages listed

Constraints / guardrails
- Read-only access; no access to raw request payloads or tenant-identifying logs beyond existing support tooling.
- Metrics should remain aggregated (avoid tenant_id dimension) per Observability standards.

Approvals needed
- SRE sign-off (dashboards are safe for Support): Rafael Mendes
- Observability standards sign-off / RBAC ownership: Allison Grant
- Confluence permissions for oncall runbooks: Owen Phillips (Incident Response)

Acceptance criteria
- Support team members in okta-group support-cs can view the overload dashboards.
- Support can access the listed Confluence runbooks.
- A short internal note is posted in #support with links + what to check first (breaker open rate, shed rate, Retry-After).

Notes
Support has active customer threads where we could have avoided back-and-forth if we had this access (see linked SUP tickets).
